subject: maths
printing: Part I: First Edition April 2026; Part II: First Edition August 2026
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF
note: Part II continues the chapter numbering of Part I (Chapters 9–14). Several third-party sites list wrong Part II chapters (e.g. "Statistics", "Probability"); the titles here are from the NCERT Part II prelims PDF, first edition August 2026.

chapters.title: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

topics.title: The Cartesian coordinate system
outcomes: Learner can locate and plot points in the 2-D plane using ordered pairs and quadrants
misconceptions: Thinks (3, 2) and (2, 3) are the same point
Plots the y-coordinate along the x-axis
hooks: Seat numbers in a cinema hall; grid squares on a city map

topics.title: Distance between two points
outcomes: Learner can find the distance between two points using the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem
misconceptions: Subtracts coordinates and adds them without squaring
hooks: How far is the school from home on a grid map?

topics.title: Linear polynomials
outcomes: Learner can identify linear polynomials and evaluate them
misconceptions: Thinks 2x and x² are the same kind of term
hooks: Auto fare: base fare + rate per km

topics.title: Linear patterns and relationships
outcomes: Learner can recognise linear patterns in tables and write a rule ax + b
misconceptions: Assumes any increasing pattern is linear
hooks: Phone recharge plans: fixed + per-GB cost

topics.title: Visualising linear relationships
outcomes: Learner can plot a linear relationship and interpret slope and intercept informally
misconceptions: Thinks the graph of a linear relation must pass through the origin
hooks: Taxi fare graph vs distance

topics.title: The story of number systems
outcomes: Learner can trace the growth from counting numbers to integers and rationals, including Indian contributions (Brahmagupta’s rules for zero)
misconceptions: Believes negative numbers were always accepted
hooks: Ishango bone tally marks; Bakhshali manuscript

topics.title: Rational numbers and their density
outcomes: Learner can represent rational numbers and show there are infinitely many between any two
misconceptions: Thinks there is no number between 0.1 and 0.2
hooks: Zoom into a ruler between two millimetre marks

topics.title: Irrational numbers
outcomes: Learner can explain why √2 is irrational and construct √2 and √3 lengths geometrically
misconceptions: Believes π = 22/7 exactly
Thinks √2 = 1.414 exactly
hooks: The diagonal of a square tile; Madhava’s series for π

topics.title: Real numbers as decimals
outcomes: Learner can classify decimals as terminating, repeating or non-repeating and convert repeating decimals to fractions
misconceptions: Thinks 0.999... is less than 1
hooks: Why 1/7 gives the cyclic number 142857

topics.title: Visualising identities
outcomes: Learner can derive identities like (a + b)², (a + b + c)² and (a ± b)³ with area and volume models
misconceptions: Believes (a + b)³ = a³ + b³
hooks: Algebra tiles; cutting a cube of jaggery

topics.title: Factorisation
outcomes: Learner can factorise quadratic and cubic expressions using tiles and identities
misconceptions: Factorises x² + 5x + 6 as (x + 5)(x + 6)
hooks: Arrange tiles into a rectangle

topics.title: Simplifying rational expressions
outcomes: Learner can simplify algebraic fractions by factorising
misconceptions: Cancels terms instead of factors ((x + 2)/2 = x)
hooks: Simplify formulas used in physics later

chapters.title: I’m Up and Down, and Round and Round

topics.title: Circle definitions and symmetries
outcomes: Learner can use terms radius, chord, diameter, arc, segment and sector and describe a circle’s symmetries
misconceptions: Thinks every chord passes through the centre
hooks: Spokes and rim of a cycle wheel

topics.title: Chords, perpendicular bisectors and distances
outcomes: Learner can prove and use that the perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord and that equal chords are equidistant
misconceptions: Believes a longer chord is farther from the centre
hooks: Find the centre of a broken plate

topics.title: Angles subtended by arcs and concyclic points
outcomes: Learner can use the theorem that the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference and properties of cyclic quadrilaterals
misconceptions: Thinks angles in the same segment change with position
hooks: Best seat in a semi-circular auditorium

topics.title: Perimeter of a circle and the C/D ratio
outcomes: Learner can explain π as the constant ratio of circumference to diameter and find circumference and arc length
misconceptions: Believes π changes with the size of the circle
hooks: Measure a bangle with thread; Archimedes and Aryabhata’s value of π

topics.title: Areas of triangles and parallelograms, Heron’s formula
outcomes: Learner can find areas of triangles using base-height and Heron’s formula
misconceptions: Uses Heron’s formula with the full perimeter instead of the semi-perimeter
hooks: Area of a triangular plot from its three sides

topics.title: Area of a circle and a sector
outcomes: Learner can derive and use the area of a circle and a sector
misconceptions: Confuses 2πr and πr²
hooks: Area watered by a rotating sprinkler

topics.title: Puzzles and paradoxes on perimeter and area
outcomes: Learner can reason about shapes with equal perimeter but different area and vice versa
misconceptions: Thinks a longer boundary always encloses more area
hooks: Coastline paradox: how long is India’s coastline?

chapters.title: The Mathematics of Maybe: Introduction to Probability

topics.title: The probability scale
outcomes: Learner can place events on a 0-to-1 probability scale using words like impossible, unlikely, likely, certain
misconceptions: Believes an event is 50-50 because it either happens or it does not
hooks: Chance of rain from the IMD forecast

topics.title: Experimental and theoretical probability
outcomes: Learner can compute experimental probability from trials and compare with theoretical probability
misconceptions: Thinks after many tails, heads is "due" (gambler’s fallacy)
Believes getting a 6 on a die is harder than other numbers
hooks: Coin toss before a cricket match

topics.title: Sample spaces, events and tree diagrams
outcomes: Learner can list sample spaces, use tree diagrams for two-stage experiments and find probabilities of events
misconceptions: Treats outcomes like "sum = 7" and "sum = 2" with two dice as equally likely
hooks: Ludo with two dice

chapters.title: Predicting What Comes Next: Exploring Sequences and Progressions

topics.title: Explicit and recursive rules
outcomes: Learner can describe sequences with explicit and recursive rules
misconceptions: Believes a sequence can have only one kind of rule
hooks: Savings that grow by ₹50 each week

topics.title: Arithmetic progressions and sums
outcomes: Learner can find the nth term of an AP and the sum of the first n natural numbers
misconceptions: Uses a + nd instead of a + (n − 1)d for the nth term
hooks: Gauss and the sum 1 to 100; seats in rows of a stadium

topics.title: Geometric progressions
outcomes: Learner can identify GPs and their growth and connect them to fractals
misconceptions: Thinks a GP and AP grow the same way
hooks: The chessboard and grains of rice legend

topics.title: Propositions and converses
outcomes: Learner can state the converse of an "if-then" statement and decide whether each is true
misconceptions: Believes that if a statement is true, its converse must also be true
hooks: "if it rains, the road is wet" — is the converse true?

topics.title: Counterexamples and proof
outcomes: Learner can use a counterexample to disprove a claim and write a short logical argument
misconceptions: Thinks a few examples prove a general statement
hooks: Fermat’s claim about 2^(2^n) + 1 being prime

topics.title: Weighted averages and mixtures
outcomes: Learner can compute weighted averages and explain why the average of averages can mislead
misconceptions: Averages two class averages without considering class sizes
hooks: Mixing two grades of tea; combined result of two sections

topics.title: Visualising composition: stacked columns and alternatives to pie charts
outcomes: Learner can draw and interpret stacked column charts and choose a suitable chart for composition data
misconceptions: Believes a pie chart is always the best way to show parts of a whole
hooks: How students commute: walk, bus, cycle across classes

topics.title: What is an algorithm
outcomes: Learner can describe a step-by-step procedure precisely, such as digit-by-digit addition
misconceptions: Thinks an algorithm must be a computer program
hooks: A recipe for making poha as an algorithm

topics.title: Algorithms for the greatest common divisor
outcomes: Learner can compare different algorithms for GCD, including Euclid’s subtraction algorithm
misconceptions: Believes all correct algorithms are equally fast
hooks: Cutting the largest equal squares from a rectangular sheet

topics.title: Analysing and improving algorithms
outcomes: Learner can count the steps an algorithm takes and suggest improvements
misconceptions: Thinks a shorter-looking algorithm always runs faster
hooks: Finding a name in a sorted register vs an unsorted one

topics.title: Properties of parallelograms
outcomes: Learner can prove properties of parallelograms (opposite sides, angles, diagonals) using congruence
misconceptions: Assumes a property from a diagram without proof
hooks: Folding stands and scissor lifts keep sides parallel

topics.title: Mid-point theorem and medians
outcomes: Learner can use the mid-point theorem and show that medians of a triangle meet at a point
misconceptions: Thinks the centroid is the midpoint of a median
hooks: Balance a cardboard triangle on a pencil tip

topics.title: Tiling with any quadrilateral
outcomes: Learner can explain why any quadrilateral can tile the plane
misconceptions: Believes only regular shapes tile
hooks: Design an irregular tile pattern for a courtyard

topics.title: Linear equations in two variables
outcomes: Learner can write a situation as ax + by + c = 0 and find several solutions
misconceptions: Thinks a linear equation in two variables has only one solution
hooks: Buying pens and pencils for exactly ₹100

topics.title: Graph of a linear equation
outcomes: Learner can plot the graph of a linear equation and interpret points on it as solutions
misconceptions: Believes points off the line can also be solutions
hooks: Graph of total cost vs number of items

topics.title: Slope and slope-intercept form
outcomes: Learner can find the slope of a line and write y = mx + c
misconceptions: Computes slope as run over rise
hooks: Steepness of a ghat road; wheelchair ramps

chapters.title: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume

topics.title: Cuboids, cubes and cylinders
outcomes: Learner can find surface areas and volumes of cuboids, cubes and cylinders
misconceptions: Confuses surface area with volume
Uses diameter in place of radius
hooks: Paint for a room; capacity of a water tank

topics.title: Cones and pyramids
outcomes: Learner can find surface areas and volumes of cones and pyramids and relate them to prisms and cylinders
misconceptions: Uses vertical height instead of slant height for curved surface area
hooks: Ice-cream cones; a heap of grain at the mandi

topics.title: Spheres and hemispheres
outcomes: Learner can find surface areas and volumes of spheres and hemispheres
misconceptions: Thinks doubling the radius doubles the volume
hooks: Steel katoris as hemispheres; volume of a football
